threads.body: [General] This transfer misses Camel message copies. In Camel 2.20, `DefaultExchange.copy()` calls `Message.copy()`, and `JmsMessage.copyFrom(...)` assigns the underlying JMS message field directly rather than invoking this constructor or `setJmsMessage`. Multicast/parallel or other copied exchanges therefore lose `JmsMessageDeliveryState`; a later route falls back to an unclaimed message and can record `messaging.client.consumed.messages` again for the same physical delivery. Please also propagate the state when a `JmsMessage` is copied, and cover a JMS route that crosses a copied/parallel exchange.

threads.body: [Javaagent] This check-and-set is not atomic even though the same state is deliberately shared by the physical JMS message and Camel wrappers. Camel supports parallel route processing, so two routes can both observe `false` and both return `true`, producing duplicate consumed-message counts. Make the ownership claim atomic (for example, synchronize this method or use an atomic state transition).

threads.body: [bug] This removes consumed-message emission from process-only JMS deliveries. A pushed `MessageListener` callback has no receive operation, so `MessagingConsumerMetrics.getForOperationType()` never runs and `messaging.client.consumed.messages` is no longer emitted for that delivery. Please retain an equivalent process-side claim for push callbacks while still avoiding a second claim for receive-backed deliveries; consumed-message deduplication is tracked separately in #20214.

threads.body: [Javaagent] This `VirtualField.find` is initialized on an `inline = false` advice class. Non-inlined advice is not rewritten, so this lookup is not registered through the advice transformation and is rejected by the repository's VirtualField validation. Move the handle to a non-advice helper/singleton and have the advice reference that handle.
